title: Cleaning and calibrating a poultry incubator
subtitle: Preparing the machine between hatches to protect fertility and hatchability.
excerpt: A dirty incubator carries bacteria and mould from one hatch to the next, infecting developing embryos before they can hatch. Full disinfection between every hatch and a calibration check at the start of each season keeps infection rates low and temperature accuracy high. Both steps take under 2 hours.
sourceNotes: Gail Damerow, Storey's Guide to Raising Chickens (4th edn., 2017), incubation chapter. Practical Poultry magazine, Incubator hygiene (Oct 2021). AHDB Poultry, Incubation and Hatchery Hygiene (2019).

glossaryTerms.definition: Checking the temperature and humidity displayed by the incubator controls against a known-accurate reference thermometer and hygrometer before each hatch.
Shell fragments, membrane, fluff, and dried albumen left in an incubator after chicks hatch. A major source of bacteria and mould if not removed promptly.

content.text: Most incubation failures trace back to two causes: poor temperature accuracy and contamination. A newly cleaned, calibrated incubator removes both risks at once. The cleaning process is straightforward as long as all
is removed before disinfectant is applied.
Remove all chicks, eggs, and trays. Unplug the incubator. Allow to cool fully before handling the heating element if accessible.

Remove all loose debris by hand, then vacuum out the remaining fluff and fragments with a small handheld vacuum. Disinfectant applied over debris does not penetrate; the physical removal step is not optional.
Wash all removable components (trays, water channels, egg turners) with hot water and a food-grade detergent. Rinse thoroughly and allow to dry completely before reassembling.

Wipe all internal surfaces of the cabinet with a diluted virucidal/bactericidal disinfectant (e.g. Virkon S at label rate, or a similar product labelled for poultry hatcheries). Follow the contact time specified on the label before wiping off.
Leave the incubator open to air out in a dust-free location for 24 hours before storing or setting up for the next hatch.
confirms that the incubator display matches the actual temperature at egg level. Cheap sensors drift; a 0.5 C gap matters over a 21-day incubation.
Set the incubator to your target temperature (37.5 C for still-air, 37.7 C for fan-assisted for most poultry). Allow 4 hours to stabilise before reading.
Place a reference thermometer at egg level and compare it with the display. Adjust the control until both agree on the target temperature.
Check humidity using a separate hygrometer if your incubator has humidity control. Target 45 to 55% relative humidity for most poultry through days 1 to 18, rising to 65 to 70% at lockdown.

attrs.cue: Membrane and shell fragments are stuck firmly to the incubator floor
attrs.cause: Dried albumen acts as a glue; normal after a busy hatch
attrs.fix: Soak the stuck areas with a damp cloth for 5 to 10 minutes before scraping. Do not use a sharp tool that could damage the incubator floor or sensors.

attrs.cue: Incubator temperature fluctuates by 1 C or more
attrs.cause: Faulty thermostat, or the incubator is placed in a location with inconsistent ambient temperature
attrs.fix: Move the incubator away from windows, direct sunlight, and external doors. If fluctuation persists in a stable environment, the thermostat needs replacing or the incubator should be serviced.
